frb_001: You can recognise it as the tallest tree in Germany, 67.85 metres, among several other Douglas firs from the same 1913 planting trial. It stands at the end of a signed trail in the Mühlwald.
frb_002: You can recognise it by standing on the corner plot beside the public sculpture Kaichina Doll. It stands at Wilhelmstraße and Moltkestraße, Sedanquartier.
frb_003: You can recognise it by its gnarled shape and fan-shaped leaves turning gold each autumn, standing on a former parking lot. It stands on Bernhardstraße, towards Habsburgerstraße.
frb_004: You can recognise it by standing alone at an ordinary street corner in northern Freiburg. It stands at Einsteinstraße and Hermann-Mitsch-Straße.
frb_005: You can recognise it by its soft, red-brown, fire-resistant bark, protected from parked cars by bollards around its roots. It stands off Starkenstraße, near number 26.
frb_006: You can recognise them by the pair standing together beside the path, the oldest protected trees in Freiburg. They stand on the Lorettoberg, beside the Kapellenweg.
frb_007: You can recognise it by its height, 38 metres, the tallest protected tree in Freiburg, at the edge of a walled monastery garden. It stands on Kartauserstrasse, by the Kartause.
